purpose: Kobler de håndredigerte årsakskjedene og historiografiske debattene i de 18 generator-eide Historie-kapitlene til eksplisitt akademisk sekundærlitteratur. Laget er orienterende forskningsgrunnlag for fortolkning og forklaring; det erstatter ikke claim-spesifikke primærkilder eller stedsevidens.

sources.title: The Landscape of History: How Historians Map the Past
sources.source_location: Chapter 3, ‘Structure and Process’, pp. 35–52; Chapter 6, ‘Causation, Contingency, and Counter Factuals’, pp. 91–110.
sources.authority: Academic monograph in historical theory and method from a university press.
sources.limitations: Methodological orientation for causal reasoning, contingency and structure/process; it does not substantiate domain-specific historical facts.

sources.title: The British Industrial Revolution in Global Perspective
sources.source_location: Chapter 5, ‘Why England succeeded’, pp. 106–132; Chapter 6, ‘Why was the Industrial Revolution British?’, pp. 135–155.
sources.authority: Research monograph in economic and social history from a university press.
sources.limitations: Britain-centred causal account; must be contrasted with social, labour, gender and non-British evidence before being generalized.

sources.title: Hitler's Empire: Nazi Rule in Occupied Europe
sources.source_location: Monograph-wide comparative analysis of occupation, collaboration, coercion, administration, population policy and local variation in Nazi-occupied Europe.
sources.authority: Synthetic secondary scholarship by a specialist historian of modern Europe.
sources.limitations: European comparative frame; Norwegian actions and institutions still require Norway-specific archival and scholarly evidence.

sources.title: Protecting Soldiers and Mothers: The Political Origins of Social Policy in the United States
sources.publisher: Belknap Press of Harvard University Press
sources.source_location: Book-wide comparative-causal argument linking state institutions, organized actors, gender and the formation of social policy.
sources.limitations: United States case; useful for causal and institutional comparison, not as direct evidence for Norwegian welfare-state chronology.

sources.title: Foreign Relations: American Immigration in Global Perspective
sources.source_location: Introduction and book-wide analysis of migrant-created transnational linkages and the relation between mobility ‘from below’ and state policy ‘from above’.
sources.limitations: US-centred empirical material; supports transnational framing but not direct claims about Norwegian migrant groups or policy.

sources.title: Between Memory and History: Les Lieux de Mémoire
sources.source_location: Representations 26, pp. 7–24; article-wide distinction between memory, history and lieux de mémoire.
sources.authority: Research article in a scholarly journal published by a university press.
sources.limitations: Developed from French memory politics; its categories must be tested rather than transferred mechanically to Norwegian cases.

sources.title: European Cities and Towns: 400–2000
sources.source_location: Chapters 12–16 on urban trends, economy, social life, culture/landscape and governance, 1800–2000; Chapter 17 conclusion, pp. 359–370.
sources.authority: Peer-reviewed university-press synthesis in European urban history.
sources.limitations: European synthetic scale; Oslo-specific planning, ownership and displacement claims require local documentation.

sources.title: Normal Accidents: Living with High-Risk Technologies
sources.source_location: Updated Princeton edition; opening analytical chapters on interactive complexity, tight coupling and system accidents, followed by comparative high-risk technology cases.
sources.authority: University-press systems analysis widely used in disaster and technology studies.
sources.limitations: Theory of technological systems, not a universal history of disasters; social vulnerability and historically specific institutions require independent evidence.

sources.title: Gender: A Useful Category of Historical Analysis
sources.source_location: The American Historical Review 91(5), pp. 1053–1075; article-wide methodological argument for gender as a category of historical analysis and relation of power.
sources.authority: Major peer-reviewed historiographical article in the discipline's flagship US journal.
sources.limitations: Analytical framework rather than a chronology of Norwegian gender, family or sexuality; historical categories must remain time- and source-specific.

sources.title: The Great Divergence: China, Europe, and the Making of the Modern World Economy
sources.source_location: Introduction; Part One, ‘A World of Surprising Resemblances’; later comparative argument on resources, colonies and paths of industrial development.
sources.authority: University-press global economic history monograph central to comparative divergence debates.
sources.limitations: Macro-comparative argument; cannot by itself establish prices, wages, ownership or value chains in a specific Norwegian case.

sources.title: A Secular Age
sources.publisher: Belknap Press of Harvard University Press
sources.source_location: Parts I–III on reform, disciplinary society and the emergence of new conditions of belief; used only for the secularization/pluralization interpretive problem.
sources.authority: University-press synthetic work on historical transformations in religion and secularity.
sources.limitations: Broad Western interpretive synthesis with philosophical ambitions; institutional change and lived religion in Norway require separate historical scholarship and sources.

sources.title: Assimilation of the Sami – Implementation and Consequences
sources.source_location: Acta Borealia 20(2), pp. 121–146; article-wide analysis of Norwegianization policy, implementation and consequences.
sources.authority: Peer-reviewed specialist article in a Nordic circumpolar-studies journal.
sources.limitations: Centres assimilation policy and its consequences; earlier contact zones, internal Sami diversity and later revitalization require additional sources and Sami scholarship.

sources.title: A Place for Stories: Nature, History, and Narrative
sources.source_location: The Journal of American History 78(4), pp. 1347–1376; article-wide analysis of environmental history, causal narrative and competing interpretations of environmental change.
sources.authority: Peer-reviewed historiographical article by an environmental historian.
sources.limitations: US case and narrative-method focus; Norwegian climate, pollution and resource histories require local datasets and research.

sources.title: Networks of Power: Electrification in Western Society, 1880–1930
sources.source_location: Chapters 4–6 on reverse salients, conflict/resolution and technological momentum; Chapters 13–14 on regional system cultures and comparative systems.
sources.authority: University-press prize-winning history of technology and large technical systems.
sources.limitations: Electrification cases cannot stand in for all sciences or technologies; domain-specific institutions, medicine, media and digital systems require their own evidence.

sources.title: Colonialism in Question: Theory, Knowledge, History
sources.source_location: Chapters 1–2 on colonial studies and historical trajectories; Chapters 4–6 on globalization, modernity, states/empires; Chapters 7–8 on labour, politics and the end of empire.
sources.authority: University-press collection of historical essays by a specialist historian of colonial Africa and empire.
sources.limitations: Conceptual and comparative scope; concrete Norwegian participation, commodity chains and decolonization links still require named actors and claim-specific sources.

sources.title: Dynamics of Contention
sources.source_location: Chapter 2, ‘Lineaments of Contention’, pp. 38–71; Chapter 3, ‘Comparisons, Mechanisms, and Episodes’, pp. 72–88.
sources.authority: University-press comparative research monograph on contentious politics and causal mechanisms.
sources.limitations: Comparative social-science framework; historical movement claims must remain grounded in period-specific organizations, media, repertoires and archives.

sources.title: A History of Archaeological Thought
sources.source_location: Second edition; book-wide history of archaeological interpretation, including culture-historical, processual and post-processual approaches and their assumptions about material culture and identity.
sources.authority: University-press disciplinary history and historiography of archaeology.
sources.limitations: Historiography of archaeological thought, not direct evidence for any Scandinavian site, chronology or population.

sources.title: The First World War, Volume I: To Arms
sources.source_location: Volume I synthetic analysis of pre-war strategy and politics, mobilization, early campaigns, war economies and the widening of the conflict beyond a purely western-European frame.
sources.authority: Large-scale scholarly synthesis from Oxford University Press by a specialist military historian.
sources.limitations: First-volume scope and military-strategic emphasis; later war years, interwar outcomes and Norwegian neutrality require additional evidence.

sources.title: The Global Cold War: Third World Interventions and the Making of Our Times
sources.source_location: Introduction and comparative chapters on superpower ideology/intervention, decolonization, revolutionary projects and local agency in Africa, Asia and Latin America.
sources.authority: University-press international-history monograph central to global Cold War historiography.
sources.limitations: Global intervention focus; Nordic security, Norwegian welfare and local postwar social history require separate scholarship and sources.

coverage.use: Setter teknologi/marked opp mot sosial og institusjonell årsaksforklaring uten å gjøre industrialisering teleologisk.
Forankrer debatten om tvang, samarbeid, tilpasning og handlekraft i komparativ okkupasjonshistorie.
Forankrer årsak mellom institusjoner, rettigheter, organisering, kjønn og sosial kontroll uten lineær fremskrittsfortelling.
Forankrer spenningen mellom nasjonal institusjonshistorie og transnasjonale forbindelser.
Forankrer skillet mellom fortid, historie, minne og institusjonalisert kulturarv.
Forankrer byendring som samspill mellom økonomi, styring, sosial struktur, landskap og kontingente valg.
Forankrer skillet mellom utløsende hendelse, systembetingelser og langsiktige sårbarheter.
Forankrer kjønn som historisk kategori og maktrelasjon framfor tidløs egenskap.
Forankrer komparativ forklaring av marked, ressurser, institusjoner og globale avhengigheter.
Forankrer sekularisering som omforming av betingelser og institusjoner, ikke automatisk lineær religionsnedgang.
Forankrer analyse av fornorskning og koloniserende statsmakt samtidig som samisk handlekraft og variasjon må bevares.
Forankrer miljø som historisk årsaksfelt uten miljødeterminisme og med eksplisitt narrativ/kausal refleksjon.
Forankrer teknologisk endring i systemer, institusjoner, kultur og politikk framfor oppfinnelse alene.
Forankrer imperium, kolonialisme, globalisering og dekolonisering uten å naturalisere Europa som sentrum.
Forankrer mobilisering i mekanismer, relasjoner, organisering og kontingens framfor misnøye alene.
Forankrer arkeologisk tolkningshistorie og skillet mellom materiell likhet, klassifikasjon, kultur og identitet.
Forankrer første verdenskrig som flerkausalt og globalt forløp uten å gjøre krigsutbrudd eller mellomkrigskrise uunngåelig.
Forankrer global Cold War-perspektiv og lokal handlekraft uten å redusere alle konflikter til supermaktsstedfortredere.
